title: Gaussian Naive Bayes
subtitle: Bayes' Theorem & Class-Conditional Contours
summary: Model each class as an axis-aligned Gaussian cloud and classify via posterior probabilities.

evaluationChart.title: Class Posterior Probability Distribution
evaluationChart.description: Displays the normalized Bayesian posterior probabilities for the active query point.

advantages: Blazingly fast O(n · d) closed-form training and instant inference.
Performs remarkably well on small datasets and high-dimensional text.
Provides explicit generative likelihoods and posterior probabilities.
limitations: Conditional independence assumption ignores feature correlations.
Gaussian assumption fails if true feature distributions are heavily skewed.
Zero-variance or rare feature issues require Laplace/var smoothing.

formulas.label: Bayes' Theorem
formulas.description: Multiplies class prior by independent Gaussian likelihoods across features.

hyperparameters.label: Variance Smoothing
hyperparameters.description: Adds stability floor to class feature variances.

codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[2.0,2.4],[2.8,3.6],[6.2,6.0],[7.0,7.3]])
y = np.array([0, 0, 1, 1])

gnb = GaussianNB().fit(X, y)
print('Posteriors:', gnb.predict_proba([[4.5, 4.5]]))
